evals.prompt: Profiled LOB column sizes across three Oracle tables migrating to Aurora PostgreSQL via AWS DMS show: (1) `audit_notes` has two `CLOB` columns whose max sizes are `12 KB` and `8 KB` (`20 KB` max combined, zero rows over `20 KB`); (2) `customer_tickets` has a primary key and `90%` of `attachment_blob` values `< 28 KB` with `10%` outliers up to `18 MB`; and (3) `medical_imaging` has uniform `150–400 MB` `BLOB`s. Select the exact DMS LOB mode, task topology, and `TargetMetadata` JSON settings for each.
evals.expected_output: Applies Step 1 Deterministic LOB Selection (`SKILL.md`): (1) `audit_notes` (`< 32 KB` Oracle limit) -> Limited LOB Mode (`LimitedSizeLobMode: true, FullLobMode: false`, calculating `LobMaxSize = (20 KB) + 10% buffer = 22 KB`); (2) `customer_tickets` (skewed distribution + Primary Key) -> Inline LOB Mode (`SupportLobs: true, FullLobMode: true, InlineLobMaxSize: 32, LimitedSizeLobMode: false`); and (3) `medical_imaging` (`> 100 MB` uniform huge LOBs) -> Full LOB Mode (`FullLobMode: true, LimitedSizeLobMode: false, LobChunkSize: 64`) isolated in its own dedicated DMS replication task so it never stalls standard tables.
expectations: Activates the dms-data-migration-execution skill

Selects Limited LOB Mode (`LimitedSizeLobMode: true`, `LobMaxSize` = max KB + 10% buffer ~= 22 KB) for `audit_notes` and Inline LOB Mode (`FullLobMode: true, InlineLobMaxSize: 32`) for `customer_tickets`
Selects Full LOB Mode (`LobChunkSize: 64`) in a dedicated isolated DMS replication task for `medical_imaging`

evals.prompt: During our `3 TB` Full Load + CDC migration to Aurora PostgreSQL, leaving secondary indexes and foreign keys enabled slowed Full Load by 6x, and when we dropped all indexes, CDC `CDCLatencyTarget` exploded to 4 hours! Give the exact 4-phase DMS staging, pause-and-index, and `< 5s` cutover protocol.
evals.expected_output: Walks through Step 4 (Target RDS Staging, Index Building & Cutover Protocol): (1) Before Full Load: disable target Multi-AZ, disable foreign keys & triggers, and omit secondary indexes; (2) Pause After Full Load: set `"StopTaskCachedChangesNotApplied": true` in `FullLoadSettings` so DMS halts immediately after Full Load before applying cached CDC, and create all Primary Keys and Secondary Indexes now (so CDC `UPDATE`/`DELETE` statements don't trigger full-table scans!); (3) Resume CDC: call `start-replication-task --start-replication-task-type resume-processing` with Batch Apply and `EnableValidation: true`; and (4) Cutover: once `CDCLatencySource` & `CDCLatencyTarget` `< 5s`, stop source writes, let lag hit `0`, re-enable Multi-AZ + FKs + triggers, reset sequences, and switch app endpoints.
expectations: Activates the dms-data-migration-execution skill
Uses `StopTaskCachedChangesNotApplied: true` to pause right after Full Load and creates Primary Keys + Secondary Indexes BEFORE resuming cached CDC (`resume-processing`)
Disables Multi-AZ/FKs/triggers during Full Load and re-enables Multi-AZ, FKs, triggers, and sequence offsets during the `< 5s` lag cutover

evals.prompt: A DMS CDC task reading from our production RDS PostgreSQL source failed 36 hours ago and nobody restarted it — now `FreeStorageSpace` on the source RDS instance dropped from `600 GB` to `28 GB` (`TransactionLogsDiskUsage` is `540 GB`)! Explain the mechanism, immediate emergency triage, and permanent parameter guardrail.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses orphaned/inactive PostgreSQL Logical Replication Slot WAL retention: when a DMS CDC task stops without dropping its slot (`pg_replication_slots` `active = false`), PostgreSQL retains every WAL segment since `restart_lsn`, filling storage until the primary DB crashes read-only! Immediate emergency steps: inspect `pg_replication_slots` (`pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)`), immediately drop the inactive slot (`SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot(...)`) if `28 GB` free disk cannot survive CDC catch-up (recovering `540 GB` WAL immediately, then re-running DMS Full Load+CDC or PITR sync) + scale storage emergency buffer; permanent guardrail: set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` in the DB Parameter Group + CloudWatch alarms on `OldestReplicationSlotLag` and `TransactionLogsDiskUsage`.
expectations: Activates the dms-data-migration-execution skill
Identifies inactive PostgreSQL logical replication slot (`pg_replication_slots` `active = false`) retaining `540 GB` of WAL and risking primary DB disk-full outage

Provides immediate emergency triage (`pg_drop_replication_slot` when disk exhaustion is imminent vs resuming) and permanent `max_slot_wal_keep_size` + `OldestReplicationSlotLag`/`TransactionLogsDiskUsage` alarms

evals.expected_output: Applies Step 2 (Replication Instance Sizing & Network Topology): (1) co-locate the DMS Replication Instance in the exact same AWS Region and Availability Zone as the target RDS/Aurora writer to eliminate cross-AZ write latency; (2) choose `dms.c6i`/`dms.c7i` for CPU-bound homogeneous Full Loads with minimal CDC state, and `dms.r6i`/`dms.r7i` (Memory-Optimized) for high-concurrency CDC, large uncommitted source transactions, Batch Apply (`BatchApplyMemoryLimit`), and Limited/Inline LOB pre-allocation (`LobMaxSize × CommitRate`); and (3) keep Single-AZ during initial testing/Full Load to save 50% cost, enabling `--multi-az` for long-running production CDC cutover phases.

evals.prompt: Compare two DMS CloudWatch alarm scenarios and give the exact root causes and fixes for each: Scenario A (`CDCLatencySource = 1,800s` and `CDCLatencyTarget = 1,805s`) vs Scenario B (`CDCLatencySource = 2s` and `CDCLatencyTarget = 2,400s`).
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes DMS pipeline latency metrics accurately: in Scenario A (`CDCLatencySource` itself is `1,800s`, and `CDCLatencyTarget` includes source lag), the bottleneck is reading changes from the source (slow Oracle LogMiner vs Binary Reader, heavy uncommitted long-running source transactions, throttled source I/O, or WAN/VPN bandwidth); whereas in Scenario B (`CDCLatencySource = 2s`, `CDCLatencyTarget = 2,400s`), source capture is healthy and the bottleneck is applying changes to the target (missing Primary Key / Unique Index on target causing full-table scans per `UPDATE`/`DELETE`, transactional single-row apply instead of `BatchApplyEnabled`, triggers/FK overhead on target, or cross-AZ target network latency).
expectations: Activates the dms-data-migration-execution skill
Diagnoses Scenario A as a source log-capture bottleneck (`CDCLatencySource` high; e.g., Oracle LogMiner vs Binary Reader, huge uncommitted source TXs, WAN bandwidth)

Diagnoses Scenario B as a target apply bottleneck (`CDCLatencySource` low, `CDCLatencyTarget` high; missing target PK/unique index causing full scans, disabled Batch Apply, active target triggers/FKs, or cross-AZ latency)
